subject: superb fairywren
title: This Bird Sings a Password to Her Eggs. Chicks That Get It Wrong Starve

scenes.text: This tiny bird teaches her chicks a password before they hatch.
From day nine of incubation, the superb fairywren mother sings to her eggs once every four minutes, a two-second trill with one special note.
When the chicks hatch, every begging call they make contains that exact note. Her mate learns it too, from her own calls.
scenes.keywords: baby birds begging nest open mouths

scenes.text: Scientists swapped eggs between nests. The hatchlings sang their foster mother's note, not their real mother's. The password is learned, inside the egg.
Why? Cuckoos sneak eggs into fairywren nests, and the cuckoo chick hatches after only a couple of days of lessons. It never learns the note.
Play the wrong call under a nest and the parents stop feeding. Many simply abandon the nest and start over. No password, no dinner.

description:
Superb fairywren mothers in Australia sing to their unhatched eggs from about day nine of incubation, once every four minutes, and each female's call carries one unique note. After hatching, the chicks' begging calls contain that note, and the parents only feed chicks that use it.
In a 2012 study in Current Biology, researchers at Flinders University swapped clutches between nests and found hatchlings copied their foster mother's note, proving it is learned in the egg. Horsfield's bronze-cuckoo chicks, laid late in incubation, miss the lessons; parents that hear the wrong call cut feeding and often abandon the nest.

first_comment: The mother also teaches the password to her mate and any helpers at the nest, so everyone bringing food knows the family code. Which animal should we decode next?
